page: Amazon Web Services i2.4xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual server powered by the Xen hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a baseline frequency of 2.5 GHz and includes a 25 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 122.0 GB of system memory, yielding 7.62 GB per core. For local storage, it bundles 3200 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is established with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average performance across several standard compute and memory metrics, alongside some notable limitations. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests fall within the average range, as do the PassMark CPU and memory scores. However, single-threaded performance is a bottleneck, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores registering in the poor category. Memory bandwidth tests show a stark contrast: read-only operations on small cached blocks achieve an average of 588.91 GB/sec, whereas large-block write bandwidth is weak at 18.74 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the i2.4xlarge lies in its older architecture, which lacks modern instruction sets like AVX-512 or AMX, resulting in weak performance for tasks like LLM inference and single-threaded decompression. Qualitatively, the server offers high local storage density and substantial memory capacity, making it a viable option for legacy database workloads, static web serving, and basic data processing where high-speed local NVMe storage is required but raw CPU single-thread performance is not the primary constraint.
